title: Microsoft Purview: delete inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departed users (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its government-cloud targets match the roadmap, and the existing priority cleanup, inactive-mailbox and auditing controls match Microsoft Learn. It distinguishes those existing capabilities from the planned feature, whose mechanism, default and specific licensing remain unpublished.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Departed users' OneDrive files can remain subject to retention settings and holds that prevent deletion.
claims.quote: If a user leaves your organization, any files that are subject to a retention policy or has a retention label will remain subject to the retention settings for the duration of the retention period specified in the policy or label.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Holds can preserve departed employees' mailboxes as inactive mailboxes.
claims.quote: An inactive mailbox (a mailbox on hold before it was deleted) will remain in a soft-deleted with hold state until the hold is removed.

claims.claim: A user's OneDrive site cannot be deleted while its Preservation Hold library contains items with unexpired retention periods.
claims.quote: When one or more items in a Preservation Hold library have an unexpired retention period, the OneDrive site for the user can't be deleted.

claims.claim: Removing all holds from an inactive mailbox results in its automatic deletion.
claims.quote: When the last hold is removed, no further action is required from you because the inactive mailbox will be automatically deleted.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete items marked as records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete items marked as regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete copies already in an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: Although priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds, the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Managing priority cleanup and enabling or disabling it requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires approval from another person in addition to its policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup policies must run in simulation before activation.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup requires a second priority cleanup administrator.
claims.quote: Once simulation results are available, ask a second priority cleanup admin to review the results ... The last person to edit the policy can't also turn it on.

claims.claim: After its last hold is removed, an inactive mailbox is permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period.
claims.quote: if you remove the final hold from an inactive mailbox the mailbox will be permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period expires.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be recovered after permanent deletion.
claims.quote: After the inactive mailbox is permanently deleted, it can't be recovered.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires auditing enabled at least one day before the first policy runs.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: The tenant priority cleanup control is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. ... select Priority cleanup settings. ... From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the tenant switch controlling creation of priority cleanup policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable configuration; "priority cleanup" "Set-PolicyConfig" "Enable"; "priority cleanup" "tenant" "cmdlet" disable. Read priority cleanup tenant-switch pages and Set-PolicyConfig syntax; no operation for this switch.

claims.claim: The OneDrive priority cleanup creation wizard opens at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup creates a priority cleanup policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the static-scope inactive-mailbox retention-policy hold removal shown in this row.
claims.quote: Searched: "inactive mailbox" "remove" "retention policy" "portal" static scope. Opened delete-an-inactive-mailbox: "You must use Exchange Online PowerShell ... You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC), or the Microsoft Purview portal for these procedures."

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds removes an inactive mailbox from entire-location retention-policy holds using older retention locations, in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Static scope: How to remove an inactive mailbox from a retention policy that's configured for the entire location ... For retention policies that use the older retention locations ... Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds

claims.claim: Auditing can be enabled at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on organisational auditing.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The priority cleanup tenant switch applies to Exchange as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off the tenant priority cleanup control prevents creation of new priority cleanup policies.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies continue functioning when the tenant control is off.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: ... Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted when the tenant control is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Existing priority cleanup policies cannot be modified when the tenant control is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Priority cleanup itself is enabled by default at tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Exchange priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and is subject to change.
claims.quote: Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be removed from a retention policy with Preservation Lock applied.
claims.quote: You won't be able to remove an inactive mailbox if the retention policy has Preservation Lock applied.

claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileRecycled is the auditing operation for deletion of a SharePoint or OneDrive item by the documented priority cleanup process.
claims.quote: Operation name of PriorityCleanupFileRecycled: The deletion of an item in SharePoint or OneDrive by priority cleanup.

claims.claim: The new feature's roles, approval requirements, safeguards and audit events are not yet published.
